intro.name: The beginning
intro.text: At the village clearing, (Potter) sets a newly shaped clay vessel upon a woven mat. A respected craftsperson inspects its rim, balance, decoration, and usefulness. Other villagers crowd around, eager to see whether it survives firing. (Potter) asks permission to enter the annual pottery contest.

choices.label: ENTER THE VESSEL IN THE PRACTICAL CRAFT CATEGORY.
ENTER THE VESSEL IN THE ARTISTIC CATEGORY.
ASK THE MASTER POTTER TO JUDGE AND TEACH.

a1.text: The Perfect Water Jar: The pot holds water without leaking and is easy to carry. The judges praise (Potter)'s skill.

text_only.reason: narrative: the judges praise the potter's skill; the tech points are the reward

a2.text: A Beautiful Sieve: The vessel is covered in tiny holes. (Potter) calls it a water jar; the judge calls it a colander. The farmers immediately request copies for washing gathered food.

text_only.reason: narrative: farmers wash gathered food in the sieve

a3.text: The Great Collapse: The unfired vessel slumps into a shapeless mound. (Potter) is mortified; an apprentice gently offers to help rebuild it.

text_only.reason: narrative: an unfired pot slumps; no structure is involved

a4.text: The Unbreakable Bowl: The bowl survives a fall onto packed earth. The judges celebrate, until someone discovers it cannot be lifted without spilling everything inside.

text_only.reason: narrative: only the judges celebrate, and briefly

a5.text: The Vessel with Two Mouths: Nobody can explain the double spout until a healer discovers it is useful for measuring small amounts of water. (Potter) becomes an unexpectedly celebrated innovator.

b1.text: The Ancestors' Faces: The carved figures are so expressive that an elder recognizes a long-dead relative. The crowd falls respectfully silent; (Potter) is awarded first place.

b2.text: The Ugliest Masterpiece: The pot resembles a lopsided crab with an enormous nose. The judges recoil; the children adore it. Years later, its likeness is found in nearly every hut.

b3.text: The Painted Catastrophe: During firing, the colors change unexpectedly. The judges call it ruined; a visiting craftsperson calls it beautiful. The village splits into rival schools of taste.

b4.text: The Stolen Pattern: (Rival) accuses (Potter) of copying a family motif. The elders investigate and discover coincidence, theft, or a shared ancestral source.

b5.text: The Speaking Pot: When the wind passes over the vessel, it makes a mournful musical note. (Potter) insists this was intentional; no one believes (potter.him/her), but the musicians beg to borrow it.

c1.text: The Merciless Critic: The judge lists twelve flaws without taking a breath. (Potter) nearly cries, then spends days improving the work. (Potter) gains a crafting-related Tech reward and new respect.

text_only.reason: rule 8: no game has a Crafting skill; the Tech reward is given

c2.text: The Critic Is Wrong: The judge condemns the shape, but a farmer demonstrates its remarkable usefulness. The judge apologizes publicly.

c3.text: The Apprentice's Triumph: A child quietly suggests reinforcing the base. The resulting pot wins; (Potter) credits the child before all.

c4.text: The Judge's Favorite: The judge praises a friend's inferior pot. Outraged competitors demand a new panel; the council may uphold or overturn the result.
